title: China’s Purges Are Working as Designed
gist: Andrew Mertha argues that Xi Jinping's purges are not a sign of Chinese Communist Party fragility but a feature of a unique discipline system that has helped the party endure, challenging the long-held view that institutionalization explained CCP resilience. Only the opening of the paywalled essay is available.

insights.claim: For two decades, scholars attributed the Chinese Communist Party's survival, unlike every communist regime in Europe, to sturdy institutions: term limits, collective leadership and merit-based promotion that moved it away from Mao-era personalist dictatorship.
insights.speaker: Andrew Mertha
insights.so_what: Investors who priced China's stability on institutional predictability need a different model now that those norms have eroded under Xi.

insights.claim: The prior view held that institutionalization made the CCP resilient enough to bounce back from external and internal shocks that had felled other socialist systems.
insights.speaker: Andrew Mertha
insights.so_what: If resilience came from institutions, their dismantling would imply fragility; the author disputes that inference.
insights.quote: which made it resilient enough to bounce back from the external and internal shocks that had felled other socialist systems

insights.claim: Xi Jinping's purges are working as designed: the party's distinctive discipline system, rather than institutional norms, has helped it endure.
insights.speaker: Andrew Mertha
insights.so_what: Do not read high-profile purges (including in the military) as signs of imminent regime instability; the base case is continued CCP control.
insights.quote: A Unique Discipline System Has Helped the Party Endure
insights.locator: China’s Purges Are Working as Designed

insights.claim: Xi Jinping has departed from the institutional model of term limits and collective leadership that scholars credited with the party's resilience.
insights.speaker: Andrew Mertha
insights.so_what: Policy direction in China is increasingly concentrated in one leader, raising key-person risk and policy-shift unpredictability for China exposure.
